data.name: AmbiguousConcatenation_Message
data.value: Both operands are `String` values; using the `&` string concatenation operator here would be more explicit about the intent here.

data.name: BitwiseOperator_Message
data.value: The result of this operation is resolved using bitwise arithmetic. This could produce unexpected results if the expectation is conventional logic here. If this isn't intentional, it could be a bug.

data.name: EmptyCodeBlock_Message
data.value: Empty code block; implement a body or consider removing it.

data.name: EmptyIfBlock_Message
data.value: Empty If block; consider reversing the conditional expression.

data.name: EnumerationOverArray_Message
data.value: Array enumeration is inefficient and would perform better with a `For...Next` construct instead, with indexed (subscript) item access.

data.name: ImplicitDateSerialConversion_Message
data.value: Implicit `DateSerial` conversion; using `VBA.DateTime` module functions to perform date and time operations would make the intent clearer while improving readability by raising the abstraction level a bit.

data.name: ImplicitLetCoercion_message
data.value: Implicit `Let` coercion (`{toType.Name}`) from `{fromType.Name}`; invoking the object's default member explicitly avoids "magic" procedure calls that are hard to follow and to fully understand without tracing obscure hidden attributes.

data.name: ImplicitNarrowingConversion_Message
data.value: Implicit narrowing conversion from a numeric type to another with a smaller range - watch out, arithmetic overflow is technically possible here.

data.name: ImplicitNumericCoercion_Message
data.value: Implicit numeric coercion (`{toType.Name}`) from `{fromType.Name}`; using an explicit type conversion function would improve the traceability of the involved data types.

data.name: ImplicitStringCoercion_Message
data.value: Implicit `String` coercion from `{fromType.Name}`; consider using an explicit type conversion (for example `CStr`) to make this operation more intentional.

data.name: ImplicitWideningConversion_Message
data.value: Implicit widening conversion from a numeric type to another with a wider range; using an explicit type conversion function here would make this operation more intentional.

data.name: LateBoundMemberAccess_Message
data.value: Late bound member access; VBA will not resolve this call until run-time, which can lead to errors that are avoidable by using a declared type more specific than `Variant` or `Object` whenever possible.

data.name: PreferErrRaiseOverErrorStatement_Message
data.value: Use the `Err.Raise` method instead of the legacy `Error` statement to raise run-time errors; like several others, this statement exists for backward compatibility with previous iterations of the BASIC programming language.

data.name: SllFailure_Message
data.value: SLL parser prediction mode failed here; if possible, rephrasing this instruction could improve language server performance.

data.name: SuspiciousValueAssignment_Message
data.value: Suspicious value assignment; since both LHS and RHS are object types, it looks like a reference assignment may have been intended. Could it be missing a `Set` keyword?

data.name: TypeCastConversion_Message
data.value: Assignment is converting the RHS object to a compatible interface type.

data.name: UnintendedConstantExpression_Message
data.value: Possibly unintended constant expression; this operation does not affect the value.

data.name: UnresolvedLateBoundMemberAccess_Message
data.value: Unresolved late bound member access; this call is likely going to raise run-time error 438 (VBR00438) at run-time.

data.name: ImplicitDeclarationsEnabled_Message
data.value: Option Explicit is not specified: a name that is not declared is not an error, and a variable is created where it is used. A misspelled name goes unnoticed.

data.name: ObsoleteCallStatement_Message
data.value: The Call keyword is obsolete: the call is the same without it.

data.name: ImplicitNonDefaultArrayBase_Message
data.value: Option Base 1 makes every array declared without a lower bound start at 1 instead of 0, while the arrays of other modules and libraries keep their own bounds. State the bounds of each array instead.

data.name: ImplicitTypeDeclarationsEnabled_Message
data.value: {0} gives a type to every name it covers that is declared without one, so the type of a variable is no longer written where it is declared. Declare each with an As clause instead.

data.name: ImplicitByRefModifier_Message
data.value: Parameter '{0}' is implicitly passed ByRef: the procedure can change the caller's variable. Write ByRef if that is intended, and ByVal otherwise.

data.name: ImplicitPublicMember_Message
data.value: '{0}' is implicitly Public. State its accessibility.

data.name: ImplicitVariantDeclaration_Message
data.value: '{0}' is implicitly declared as a Variant. State its type with an As clause (As Variant, if that is intended).

data.name: ImplicitVariantReturnType_Message
data.value: '{0}' implicitly returns a Variant. State its return type with an As clause (As Variant, if that is intended).

data.name: IntegerDataTypeDeclaration_Message
data.value: Integer is a 16-bit type that overflows at 32,767. Use a Long, unless an Integer is what a procedure or a file format expects.

data.name: ModuleScopeDimDeclaration_Message
data.value: Dim at the module level declares a Private variable. Use Private to say so.

data.name: MultilineParameterDeclaration_Message
data.value: The declaration of parameter '{0}' is split over several lines with a line continuation. Write it on one line.

data.name: MultipleDeclarations_Message
data.value: Several declarations are made by one statement, and each needs a type of its own: in Dim a, b As Long only b is a Long. Declare each on its own line.

data.name: NotAllPathsReturnValue_Message
data.value: At least one code path of '{0}' does not assign its return value: on that path, the caller gets the default value of the type (0, an empty string, Empty or Nothing).

data.name: NotAllPathsReturnValue_NeverAssigned_Message
data.value: '{0}' never assigns its return value: the caller always gets the default value of the type (0, an empty string, Empty or Nothing).

data.name: ObsoleteCommentSyntax_Message
data.value: The Rem keyword is obsolete: a comment starts with an apostrophe (').

data.name: ObsoleteErrorSyntax_Message
data.value: The Error statement is obsolete: Err.Raise raises the same error.

data.name: ObsoleteGlobalModifier_Message
data.value: Global is obsolete: it does the same as Public.

data.name: ObsoleteLetStatement_Message
data.value: The Let keyword is obsolete: the assignment is the same without it.

data.name: ObsoleteTypeHint_Message
data.value: '{0}' is written with a type-declaration character, which is obsolete: state its type with an As clause where it is declared.

data.name: ObsoleteWhileWend_Message
data.value: While...Wend is obsolete: Do While...Loop is the same loop, and the one that Exit Do can leave.

data.name: ObsoleteOnLocalErrorStatement_Message
data.value: On Local Error is obsolete: every error is local to the procedure, so Local says nothing. Use On Error.

data.name: ImplementationsShouldBePrivate_Interface_Message
data.value: '{0}' implements a member of an interface, and is Public: it exposes that member on the default interface of this class, where it does not belong. Make it Private.

data.name: ImplementationsShouldBePrivate_EventHandler_Message
data.value: '{0}' handles an event, and is Public: it can be called from outside, which an event handler never should be. Make it Private.

data.name: UseMeaningfulIdentifierNames_TooShort_Message
data.value: '{0}' is too short to say what it is: a name should have at least 3 characters.

data.name: UseMeaningfulIdentifierNames_EndsWithDigit_Message
data.value: '{0}' ends with a digit, which says it is one of several and not what makes it different from the others. Give it a name that says what it is.

data.name: UseMeaningfulIdentifierNames_NoVowel_Message
data.value: '{0}' has no vowel, and is unlikely to be a word. Give it a name that says what it is.

data.name: HungarianNotation_Message
data.value: '{0}' begins with a prefix that states its type. The type is declared: the name should say what the thing is, not what it is made of.

data.name: MisleadingByRefParameter_Message
data.value: ByRef has no effect on '{0}', the value parameter of a property Let or Set: it is always passed ByVal.
